title: Input validation
starter: A club membership form asks for a name, a date of birth and a mobile number. For each field, write down one check the program should make before it accepts the data.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: Defensive design
facts: Designing a program so it can't be broken by mistakes or deliberate misuse.
Includes input validation, authentication, anticipating misuse and maintainable code.
Assume users will do something unexpected.
stations.challenge: List three things that could go wrong if a program trusted every input.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Designing a program so it can't be broken by mistakes or deliberate misuse.
Also credit: Includes input validation, authentication, anticipating misuse and maintainable code.

questions.a: Designing a program so it copes with mistakes and misuse without breaking
Checking data entered meets certain rules before it is processed

stations.name: Type check
facts: Checks the data is the correct data type, such as a whole number rather than text.
Stops a program crashing when it tries to do maths with text.
stations.challenge: Which inputs on a sign-up form need a type check?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Checks the data is the correct data type, such as a whole number rather than text.
Also credit: Stops a program crashing when it tries to do maths with text.

questions.q: Which check would stop 'twelve' being entered as an age?
What does isnumeric() check in the code?
questions.a: Whether the input contains only digits

stations.name: Range check
facts: Checks data falls within acceptable limits, such as 1 to 3.
Anything outside the range is rejected.
stations.challenge: Suggest a sensible range check for a month and for a percentage score.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Checks data falls within acceptable limits, such as 1 to 3.
Also credit: Anything outside the range is rejected.

questions.q: Which check would reject a month of 13?
A menu accepts 1, 2 or 3. Which input should a range check reject?

stations.name: Presence check
facts: Checks that some data has been entered.
Stops required fields, like a username, being left blank.
stations.challenge: Which fields on a sign-up form must have a presence check?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Checks that some data has been entered.
Also credit: Stops required fields, like a username, being left blank.

questions.q: What does a presence check do?
questions.a: Checks that something has been entered

questions.q: Which input would fail a presence check?

stations.name: Format and length checks
facts: A format check makes sure data matches a pattern, such as DD/MM/YYYY or a postcode.
A length check makes sure data has the right number of characters, such as 11 digits for a mobile number.
stations.challenge: Describe a format check and a length check for a UK postcode.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A format check makes sure data matches a pattern, such as DD/MM/YYYY or a postcode.
Also credit: A length check makes sure data has the right number of characters, such as 11 digits for a mobile number.

questions.q: Which check makes sure a date is written as DD/MM/YYYY?
Which check makes sure a password is at least 8 characters?

stations.name: Whitelists and blacklists
facts: A whitelist stores the only inputs a program should accept, e.g. A, B and C.
A blacklist stores inputs a program should reject, e.g. illegal characters in file names.
A string can be cast to a number after it has been checked.
stations.challenge: Would you use a whitelist or a blacklist for a menu with options A, B and C? Why?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A whitelist stores the only inputs a program should accept, e.g. A, B and C.
Also credit: A blacklist stores inputs a program should reject, e.g. illegal characters in file names.

questions.a: A list of the only inputs that are allowed

questions.q: Which is the best use of a blacklist?
questions.a: Rejecting illegal characters in a file name

final.name: Final challenge: date checks

questions.q: Which type of check is each date rule?
questions.a: The field has not been left blank = Presence; The date is exactly 10 characters long = Length; The date follows the pattern DD/MM/YYYY = Format; The day, month and year are all whole numbers = Type; The month is between 1 and 12 = Range; The year is no earlier than 1920 = Range; The day is at least 01 = Range

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
